Artemis II was a crewed lunar flyby mission that took place from April 1 to April 11, 2026.
NASA operated the Artemis II mission as the first crewed flight of the Artemis program and the Space Launch System.
The Artemis II crew consisted of four astronauts: Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen.
Victor Glover became the first person of color, Christina Koch the first woman, and Jeremy Hansen the first non-American to travel around the Moon during Artemis II.
Reid Wiseman was the oldest person to travel beyond low Earth orbit and around the Moon on the Artemis II mission.
The Artemis II spacecraft, named Integrity by the crew, was manufactured by Lockheed Martin for the Orion module and Airbus for the European Service Module.
The Artemis II mission launched from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B on April 1, 2026, at 22:35:12 UTC aboard an SLS rocket.
Artemis II traveled a total distance of 700,237 miles (1,126,922 km) during its nine-day mission duration.
The Artemis II crew reached a maximum distance of 252,756 miles (406,771 km) from Earth, breaking the previous Apollo 13 record.
Artemis II performed a lunar flyby on April 6, 2026, with a closest approach of 4,067 miles (6,545 km) from the far side of the Moon.
The Artemis II crew observed a solar eclipse lasting 57 minutes and photographed the full Earth disk for the first time since the Apollo program.
Artemis II was recovered by the USS John P. Murtha in the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego on April 11, 2026.
The Artemis II mission included the AVATAR and ARCHeR payloads to study crew health and tissue analog responses in deep space.
Artemis II demonstrated optical communications using the O2O system, achieving a downlink rate of up to 260 megabits per second.
The Artemis II zero-gravity indicator mascot named Rise was designed by eight-year-old Lucas Ye and flown on the mission.
